record.original_question: What relationship, if any, does the maximum likelihood degree of an algebraic statistical model have to the convergence properties of numerical statistical algorithms such as iterative proportional scaling and the EM algorithm?

evidence.quote: It is hoped that the ML degree is related to convergence properties of numerical algorithms used by statisticians, such as iterative proportional scaling or the EM algorithm, but no systematic study in this direction has yet been undertaken.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{M} \subset \Delta_{n-1}$ be an algebraic statistical model, that is, the intersection with the probability simplex of an irreducible algebraic variety $V \subset \mathbb{C}^n$. Given a data vector $u = (u_1,\dots,u_n) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^n$, the maximum likelihood estimation problem on $\mathcal{M}$ consists of maximizing the log-likelihood $\ell_u(p) = \sum_i u_i \log p_i$ over $p \in \mathcal{M}$. The maximum likelihood degree (ML degree) of $\mathcal{M}$ is defined as the number of complex critical points of $\ell_u$ on the smooth locus of $V$ for generic $u$; equivalently, it is the degree of the likelihood correspondence projecting onto data space.

Two classical iterative numerical procedures for approximating maximum likelihood estimates are:
(i) Iterative proportional scaling (also known as iterative proportional fitting), used for hierarchical/log-linear models, which cyclically rescales an estimate so that selected marginals match the empirical marginals;
(ii) The EM algorithm, which alternates between forming the expected complete-data log-likelihood given current parameters and maximizing it.

Determine whether there is a precise mathematical relationship between the ML degree of $\mathcal{M}$ and the convergence properties (e.g., rate of convergence, number of attracting fixed points, basin structure, or global convergence) of iterative proportional scaling and/or the EM algorithm applied to maximum likelihood estimation on $\mathcal{M}$. In particular, formulate and prove (or disprove) quantitative statements connecting the ML degree to such convergence behavior.
artifact.status_search_result: No systematic theory linking the ML degree of an algebraic statistical model to the convergence behavior of iterative proportional scaling or the EM algorithm appears to be established. Convergence results for EM (monotone increase, possible local-maximum trapping) and IPS (convergence under positivity and model conditions) are well-studied, but a direct, general quantitative relationship to the ML degree was not identified in available sources. Status appears unverified/unknown.

status_evidence.title: Expectation–maximization algorithm - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: EM may converge to a local maximum of the observed data likelihood function, depending on starting values; no guarantee exists that the sequence converges to a maximum likelihood estimator.
status_evidence.claim: EM convergence is only to local maxima in general, with no general quantitative link to ML degree noted.

status_evidence.title: Iterative proportional fitting - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: If all observed values are strictly positive, existence and uniqueness of MLEs and therefore convergence is ensured.
status_evidence.claim: IPS has convergence guarantees under standard hypotheses, with no explicit connection to ML degree mentioned.

status_evidence.title: Iterative proportional scaling revisited
status_evidence.snippet: A modern optimization perspective on big count data, focusing on convergence rate analysis without invoking the algebraic ML degree.
status_evidence.claim: Recent IPS analyses use convex-optimization tools rather than ML degree.

status_evidence.title: On some algorithms for estimation in Gaussian graphical models
status_evidence.snippet: Survey/comparison of estimation algorithms for graphical models.
status_evidence.claim: No general theorem relating ML degree to algorithmic convergence is asserted.
